abstract: Accurate termination of protein synthesis is paramount for the integrity of the cellular proteome, yet the dynamics and fidelity of ribosome termination remain poorly understood. Here, we establish a profiling strategy to capture terminating ribosomes in mammalian cells and reveal a substantial heterogeneity in ribosome pausing at individual stop codons. We identify a sequence motif upstream of the stop codon that promotes termination pausing, a finding supported by massively parallel reporter assays. Unexpectedly, reduced termination pausing increases the likelihood of stop codon slippage, giving rise to proteins with heterogeneous C-terminal extensions. Mechanistically, we show that sequence-dependent termination pausing is consistent with post-decoding mRNA scanning by the 3' end of 18 S rRNA. We further uncover tissue-specific patterns of termination pausing that correlate with the stoichiometry of Rps26, which potentially modulates mRNA:rRNA interactions. Together, these results suggest termination pausing as a distinct translational signature shaped by mRNA sequence contexts, ribosome heterogeneity, and cell type-specific translational control.
